newsitem.title: USA: Sears says cooperating with U.S. prosecutors.
newsitem.headline: Sears says cooperating with U.S. prosecutors.

text.p: A Sears, Roebuck and Co spokeswoman said on Thursday the company was cooperating with federal prosecutors in a probe of the Chicago-based retailer.
"We are cooperating," Sears spokeswoman Paula Davis said in a telephone interview. "We have no further comment."
U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts, Donald Stern, said that a federal investigation into Sears's practice of collecting debts from its once-bankrupt credit card customers was continuing.

The company earlier this month admitted that it exercised "flawed legal judgement" and would refund tens of millions of dollars it collected from bankrupt credit card holders around the country, which could cost it tens of millions of dollars.

In a deal with the U.S. Attorney's office, Sears agreed to an entry of a preliminary injunction which would halt the nationwide practice and has agreed to an audit of debtors who have been hurt by its conduct. ((--Boston bureau, 617-367-4106))
